data.title: Gens Aurea: Strong Growth, Store Expansion and Attractive Valuation Support €17 Target
data.description:
Gens Aurea S.p.A., the Consumer Cyclical sector company, was revisited by a Wall Street analyst on November 19. Analyst Andrea Zampaloni from Alantra Equities reiterated a Buy rating on the stock and has a €17.00 price target.

Andrea Zampaloni gave his rating based on several factors, including Gens Aurea’s strong third-quarter sales growth despite heat-related footfall weakness and lower gold prices. Buy-Sell activity and regional results indicated further market-share gains, while resilient gross margins supported earnings quality. The faster store rollout, with 581 locations already operating and further openings planned, provides a clear foundation for continued expansion.
Cash generation remained healthy despite taxes, IPO expenses and working-capital needs, and the first interim dividend signals management’s commitment to shareholder returns. Confirmed profit guidance, ongoing double-digit trading growth and potential working-capital benefits support confidence in the outlook. At 4.5x expected FY27 EV/EBITDA and 7.2x forward P/E, the shares appear attractively valued, with the €17 target implying substantial upside from the current price.

data.title: Sa Sa’s Profitability Rebounds on Strong Sales and Cost Control; Buy Rating Maintained with HKD1.69 Price Target Unchanged
data.description:
In a report released on November 20, Mavis Hui from DBS reiterated a Buy rating on Sa Sa International Holdings Limited, with a price target of HK$1.69.

Mavis Hui gave her Buy rating based on Sa Sa’s strong first-half FY27 performance, with revenue growth, a richer exclusive-brand mix and tighter cost control driving a sharp improvement in profitability. Hong Kong and Macao benefited from rising tourist spending and store productivity, while Southeast Asia improved and Mainland China’s reduced low-margin B2B exposure supported regional earnings quality.

The positive outlook is reinforced by accelerating sales in October and mid-November, rapid payback from new stores, and a debt-free balance sheet with ample liquidity to fund expansion. With the shares trading at about 11x forward earnings and offering a dividend yield above 6.4%, Hui views the risk-reward as attractive and maintains the unchanged HKD1.69 price target.

data.title: Halneuron’s Strong Phase 2b Results Support Buy Rating; Price Target Unchanged at $12
data.description:
In a report released today, Sean Lee CFA from H.C. Wainwright maintained a Buy rating on Dogwood Therapeutics, with a price target of $12.00.

Sean Lee CFA gave his Buy rating based on several factors, led by Halneuron’s successful Phase 2b trial in chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy. The treatment produced a substantially higher rate of patients achieving meaningful pain relief than placebo, with benefits emerging early and persisting through the assessment period. Positive results across pain, functional, and patient-reported measures further support the drug’s potential in an indication with no FDA-approved treatment.

Halneuron also demonstrated favorable tolerability, strong study completion, and benefits across all planned patient subgroups, strengthening its commercial prospects. Management’s planned FDA engagement, potential Breakthrough Therapy application, and two Phase 3 studies provide a credible development pathway, although a bridging study may be needed for the synthetic formulation. The price target remains unchanged at $12, reflecting the analyst’s continued confidence in the program’s risk-reward profile.

data.title: Bird Construction: Kel-Gor Acquisition Drives Growth and Margin Expansion; Price Target Raised to $105
data.description:
Analyst John Gibson CFA of BMO Capital reiterated a Buy rating on Bird Construction, boosting the price target to C$105.00.

John Gibson CFA’s rating is based on Bird Construction’s acquisition of Kel-Gor, which adds more than $250 million in expected revenue, higher-margin industrial services, and substantial maintenance and turnaround work. The transaction also expands Bird’s self-performed capabilities across energy, infrastructure, and data-centre markets while creating opportunities to sell services through its broad customer relationships.

The deal is expected to produce mid-single-digit EPS accretion, lift EBITDA margins, and help Bird approach 9% full-year margins by 2028, while the equity financing preserves capacity for further growth. Gibson also credited Bird’s established acquisition record and raised estimates, increasing the price target from $100 to $105, which supported the Buy view despite the shares’ strong recent performance.

In another report released today, CIBC also maintained a Buy rating on the stock with a C$100.00 price target.
